long_biography.plain_text:
After studying industrial engineering at Northeastern University in Boston, Bin Laden joined the company established by his father. He rose to senior management in Saudi Binladin Group and represented it during negotiations over Beirut's postwar reconstruction. During a later restructuring, he was one of two family owners chosen for the five-member management committee.

His subsequent appointments placed him across businesses in the Middle East. He chaired Binladin Group and accepted directorships involving cement, tourism and agriculture. At Talaat Moustafa Group Holding, an Egyptian developer, he serves in an oversight capacity rather than daily management. Together, these positions show how he combined stewardship of family industrial wealth with governance responsibilities outside the original enterprise.
